label: R-12Hm-Pm
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R-12Hm-Pm}(i) Theorem \ref{TR} provides a type of sharp power mean
bounds $M_{p_{0}}\left( 1-x;b/c\right) $ for the hypergeometric mean $\left[
F\left( -a,b;c;x\right) \right] ^{1/a}$, which is sharp at $x=0$. For
convenience, we call them \textquotedblleft the first type of power mean
bounds\textquotedblright . The inequalities (\ref{Hm>Pm-p}) and (\ref 
{Hm<Pm-p}) for $p=p_{0}$ can be abbreviated as by \textquotedblleft the
first Hm$>$Pm inequality\textquotedblright\ and \textquotedblleft the first
Hm$<$Pm inequality\textquotedblright , respectively, or be collectively
called \textquotedblleft the first Hm-Pm inequality
(inequalities)\textquotedblright .

(ii) Similarly, if the hypergeometric mean $\left[ F\left( -a,b;c;x\right)  
\right] ^{1/a}$ has the sharp power mean bounds $M_{p_{0}^{\ast }}\left(
1-x;b/c\right) $ which is sharp at $x=1$, then we call them
\textquotedblleft the second type of power mean bounds\textquotedblright .
The inequalities (\ref{Hm>Pm-p}) and (\ref{Hm<Pm-p}) for $p=p_{0}^{\ast }$
can be abbreviated as by \textquotedblleft the second Hm${>}$Pm
inequality\textquotedblright\ and \textquotedblleft the second Hm${<}$Pm
inequality\textquotedblright , respectively, or be collectively called
\textquotedblleft the second Hm-Pm inequality
(inequalities)\textquotedblright .

label: T-YT
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T-YT}Suppose that $a<1$, $b>0$ and $c>\max \left\{ -a,b\right\} $.
Let $p_{0}$ and $p_{0}^{\ast }$ be defined by (\ref{p0}) and (\ref{p0*}),
respectively.

(i) If $a-b+c\geq p_{0}$, then the first Hm${>}$Pm inequality holds for $ 
x\in \left( 0,1\right) $ if and only if $c\geq 2b$.

(ii) If $a-b+c<p_{0}$, then the first Hm${>}$Pm inequality holds for $x\in
\left( 0,1\right) $ if and only if $a-b+c>0$, $c\geq 2b$ and $p_{0}\leq
p_{0}^{\ast }$.

(iii) If $a-b+c\leq p_{0}$, then the first Hm${<}$Pm inequality holds for $ 
x\in \left( 0,1\right) $ if and only if $c\leq 2b$.

(iv) If $a-b+c>p_{0}$, then the first Hm${<}$Pm inequality holds for $x\in
\left( 0,1\right) $ if and only if $c\leq 2b$ and $p_{0}\geq p_{0}^{\ast }$.

label: Cj-BRT
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{Cj-BRT}Let $a\leq 1$, $b>0$\ and $c>b>0$. If $c\geq \max \left\{
1-2a,2b\right\} $, then the second Hm${<}$Pm inequality holds for all $x\in
\left( 0,1\right) $. If $c\leq \min \left\{ 1-2a,2b\right\} $, then the
second Hm${>}$Pm inequality holds for all $x\in \left( 0,1\right) $.

label: T-BRT
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{T-BRT}Suppose $a\in (-1,1)$. If $a>-1/2$, then for all $r\in (0,1)$, 
\begin{equation*}
M_{\lambda }\left( 1-r,\frac{1}{2}\right) <\left[ F\left( -a,1;2;r\right)  
\right] ^{1/a}<M_{\mu }\left( 1-r,\frac{1}{2}\right)
\end{equation*} 
if $\lambda \leq \left( a+2\right) /3$ (sharp) and $\mu \geq \left( a\ln
2\right) /\ln \left( 1+a\right) $ (sharp). If $a<-1/2$, then the above
double inequality holds for all $r\in (0,1)$ if $\lambda \leq \left( a\ln
2\right) /\ln \left( 1+a\right) $ (sharp) and $\mu \geq \left( a+2\right) /3$
(sharp).

label: R-p0*><p0
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{R-p0*><p0}Usually, It is rather complicated to compare $p_{0}^{\ast }$
with $p_{0}$ by analytical technique. However, there provides a simple
discrimination method in \cite[Remark 2 and Theorem 2.1] 
{Yang-arXiv:2610.10581}:

If $c\geq \left( \leq \right) 2b$ and $\delta \left( p_{0}\right)
=a-b+c-p_{0}\geq \left( \leq \right) 0$, then 
\begin{equation*}
C_{p_{0}}=\left( 1-\frac{b}{c}\right) ^{-1/p_{0}}\left[ \frac{\Gamma \left(
c\right) \Gamma \left( c+a-b\right) }{\Gamma \left( c+a\right) \Gamma \left(
c-b\right) }\right] ^{1/a}>\left( <\right) 1,
\end{equation*} 
which implies $p_{0}^{\ast }\geq \left( \leq \right) p_{0}$.

label: L-b=1,c=2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L-b=1,c=2}Let $a\in \left( -1,1\right) $ and $\left( b,c\right)
=\left( 1,2\right) $. Then

(i) $p_{0}=\left( a+c\right) /\left( c+1\right) <\left( >\right) p_{0}^{\ast
}$ if $a>\left( <\right) -1/2$.

(ii) $\delta \left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =a-b+c-p_{0}^{\ast }>\left(
<\right) 0$ if $a>\left( <\right) -1/2$;

(ii) $\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =-\left( c+3\right)
\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) ^{2}+2\left( 2a-2b+2c+ab\right) p_{0}^{\ast
}-a\left( a+c\right) >0$ if $a>-1/2$.

(iii) $\gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$ if $a\in \left(
-1,-1/2\right) $
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) We have 
\begin{equation*}
p_{0}=\frac{a+c}{1+c}=\frac{a+2}{3}\text{ \ and \ }p_{0}^{\ast }=\frac{a\ln
\left( 1-b/c\right) }{\ln \frac{\Gamma \left( c\right) \Gamma \left(
c+a-b\right) }{\Gamma \left( c+a\right) \Gamma \left( c-b\right) }}=\frac{ 
a\ln 2}{\ln \left( a+1\right) }.
\end{equation*} 
Then 
\begin{equation*}
\delta \left( p_{0}\right) =a-1+2-\frac{a+2}{3}=\frac{2a+1}{3}.
\end{equation*} 
Since $c-2b=0$ and $\delta \left( p_{0}\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ if $ 
a>\left( <\right) -1/2$, by Remark \ref{R-p0*><p0}, $p_{0}^{\ast }>\left(
<\right) p_{0}\ $if $a>\left( <\right) -1/2$, which proves the first
assertion.

(ii) We have 
\begin{equation*}
\delta \left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =a-b+c-p_{0}^{\ast }=1+a-\frac{a\ln 2}{ 
\ln \left( a+1\right) }=\frac{h_{1}\left( a\right) }{\ln \left( a+1\right) },
\end{equation*} 
where 
\begin{equation*}
h_{1}\left( a\right) =\left( 1+a\right) \ln \left( a+1\right) -a\ln 2.
\end{equation*} 
Differentiation yileds that $h_{1}^{\prime \prime }\left( a\right) =1/\left(
a+1\right) >0$. This in combination with the facts that $h_{1}\left(
-1/2\right) =h\left( 0\right) =0$ and $h_{1}\left( -1^{+}\right)
=h_{1}\left( 1\right) =\ln 2>0$ leads to that $h_{1}\left( a\right) >0$ for $ 
a\in \left( -1,-1/2\right) \cup \left( 0,1\right) $ and $h_{1}\left(
a\right) <0$ for $a\in \left( -1/2,0\right) $. It thus follows that $\delta
\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$ for $a\in \left( -1/2,1\right) $ and $\delta
\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) <0$ for $a\in \left( -1,-1/2\right) $.

(iii) We have 
\begin{equation*}
\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =-\frac{a}{\ln ^{2}\left(
a+1\right) }h_{2}\left( a\right) ,
\end{equation*} 
where 
\begin{equation*}
h_{2}\left( a\right) =\left( a+2\right) \ln ^{2}\left( a+1\right) -2\left(
\ln 2\right) \left( 3a+2\right) \ln \left( a+1\right) +5a\ln ^{2}2.
\end{equation*} 
Differentiation yileds 
\begin{eqnarray*}
h_{2}^{\prime }\left( a\right)  &=&\ln ^{2}\left( a+1\right) -2\frac{\left(
3\ln 2-1\right) a+3\ln 2-2}{a+1}\ln \left( a+1\right)  \\
&&-2\frac{3a+2}{a+1}\left( \ln 2\right) +5\ln ^{2}2, \\
\frac{\left( a+1\right) ^{2}}{2\left( 3a+4\right) }h_{2}^{\prime \prime
}\left( a\right)  &=&\frac{a+2+a\ln \left( a+1\right) }{4+3a}-\ln
2=h_{3}\left( a\right) , \\
\left( 3a+4\right) ^{2}h_{3}^{\prime }\left( a\right)  &=&4\ln \left(
a+1\right) +\frac{3a^{2}+2a-2}{a+1}=h_{4}\left( a\right) , \\
h_{4}^{\prime }\left( a\right)  &=&\frac{\left( a+2\right) \left(
3a+4\right) }{\left( a+1\right) ^{2}}>0\text{ for }a\in \left( -1,1\right)
\text{.}
\end{eqnarray*}

Since $h_{4}\left( -1/2\right) =-4\ln 2-9/2<0$ and $h_{4}\left( 1\right)
=4\ln 2+3/2>0$, there is an $a_{3}\in \left( -1/2,1\right) $ such that $ 
h_{4}\left( a\right) <0$ for $a\in \left( -1/2,a_{3}\right) $ and $ 
h_{4}\left( a\right) >0$ for $a\in \left( a_{3},1\right) $. Therefore, $ 
h_{3}\left( a\right) $ is decreasing on $\left( -1/2,a_{3}\right) $ and
increasing on $\left( a_{3},1\right) $, which together with $h_{3}\left(
-1/2\right) =\left( 3-4\ln 2\right) /5>0$ and $h_{3}\left( 1\right)
=-3\left( \ln 4-1\right) /7<0$ indicates that there is an $a_{2}\in \left(
-1/2,1\right) $ such that $h_{3}\left( a\right) >0$ for $a\in \left(
-1/2,a_{2}\right) $ and $h_{3}\left( a\right) <0$ for $a\in \left(
a_{2},1\right) $. This implies that $h_{2}^{\prime }\left( a\right) $ is
increasing on $\left( -1/2,a_{2}\right) $ and decreasing on $\left(
a_{2},1\right) $, which in conjection with $h_{2}^{\prime }\left(
-1/2\right) =4\left( 3\ln 2-2\right) \left( \ln 2\right) >0$ and $ 
h_{2}^{\prime }\left( 1\right) =-2\ln 2<0$ indicates that there is an $ 
a_{1}\in \left( -1/2,1\right) $ such that $h_{2}^{\prime }\left( a\right) >0$
for $a\in \left( -1/2,a_{1}\right) $ and $h_{2}^{\prime }\left( a\right) <0$
for $a\in \left( a_{1},1\right) $. Since $h_{2}\left( -1/2\right) =0$ and $ 
h_{2}\left( 1\right) =-2\ln ^{2}2$, we see that there is an $a_{0}\in \left(
-1/2,1\right) $ such that $h_{2}\left( a\right) >0$ for $a\in \left(
-1/2,a_{0}\right) $ and $h_{2}\left( a\right) <0$ for $a\in \left(
a_{0},1\right) $. Due to $h_{2}\left( 0\right) =0$, we find that $a_{0}=0$.
We thus conclude that $\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$ for
$a\in \left( -1/2,1\right) $.

(iv) We have 
\begin{equation*}
\gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =-\left( a+2-3p_{0}^{\ast }\right)
\left( 2a-p_{0}^{\ast }\right) =3\left( p_{0}-p_{0}^{\ast }\right) \left(
\frac{a\ln 2}{\ln \left( a+1\right) }-2a\right) .
\end{equation*} 
It has been shown in the first part of this lemma that $\left(
p_{0}-p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$ for $a\in \left( -1,-1/2\right) $; since $ 
a/\ln \left( a+1\right) >0$ for all $a>-1$, it is readily seen that $\left(
a\ln 2\right) /\ln \left( a+1\right) -2a>0$ for $a\in \left( -1,-1/2\right) $ 
. Then $\gamma _{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$ for $a\in \left(
-1,-1/2\right) $.

This completes the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
The first inequality of \ref{F-a,1,2<>} was proved in \cite[Example 1] 
{Yang-arXiv:2610.10581}. We prove the second one.

(i) When $a\in \left( -1/2,1\right) $, by Lemma \ref{L-b=1,c=2}, $ 
p_{0}^{\ast }>p_{0}$, $\delta \left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$, $\delta
\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$. Using Theorem \ref{MT-3} gives 
\begin{equation*}
\left[ F\left( -a,1;2;x\right) \right] ^{1/a}<M_{p_{0}^{\ast }}\left( 1-x, 
\frac{1}{2}\right)
\end{equation*} 
for $x\in \left( 0,1\right) $.

(ii) When $a\in \left( -1,-1/2\right) $, by Lemma \ref{L-b=1,c=2}, $ 
p_{0}^{\ast }<p_{0}$, $\delta \left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) <0$, $\gamma
_{1}\left( p_{0}^{\ast }\right) >0$. Using Theorem \ref{MT-4} gives 
\begin{equation*}
M_{p_{0}^{\ast }}\left( 1-x,\frac{1}{2}\right) <\left[ F\left(
-a,1;2;x\right) \right] ^{1/a}
\end{equation*} 
for $x\in \left( 0,1\right) $.
head: environment

label: Hm-Mp0-a=0
title: Remark
body_md:
Letting $a=0$ in Corollary \ref{C1} gives 
\begin{equation}
M_{2/3}\left( 1-x,\frac{1}{2}\right) <\lim_{a\rightarrow 0}\left[ F\left(
-a,1;2;x\right) \right] ^{1/a}<M_{\ln 2}\left( 1-x,\frac{1}{2}\right)
\label{Hm-Mp0-a=0}
\end{equation} 
for $x\in \left( 0,1\right) $ with the best constants $p_{0}=2/3$ and $ 
p_{0}^{\ast }=\ln 2$. Note that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\lim_{a\rightarrow 0}\left[ F\left( -a,1;2;x\right) \right] ^{1/a} &=&\exp  
\left[ -\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{x^{n}}{n\left( n+1\right) }\right]  \\
&=&\exp \left[ -\frac{\left( 1-x\right) \ln \left( 1-x\right) }{x}-1\right]
=I\left( 1,1-x\right) ,
\end{eqnarray*} 
where $I\left( 1,1-x\right) $ is the exponential mean of $1$ and $\left(
1-x\right) \in \left( 0,1\right) $. Then the double inequality (\ref 
{Hm-Mp0-a=0}) can be written as 
\begin{equation*}
M_{2/3}\left( x,\frac{1}{2}\right) <I\left( 1,x\right) <M_{\ln 2}\left( x, 
\frac{1}{2}\right)
\end{equation*} 
for $x\in \left( 0,1\right) $, which was proven in \cite 
{Pittinger-UBPEFSMF-680-1980} (see also \cite{Stolarsky-AMM-87-1980} \cite 
{Yang-MIA-10-2007}).

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{P-sgnS}Let $S\left( x\right) $ be an NP-type power series converging
on the interval $\left( 0,r\right) $ ($r>0$). (i) If $S\left( r^{-}\right)
\leq 0$, then $S\left( x\right) <0$ for all $x\in \left( 0,r\right) $. (ii)
If $S\left( r^{-}\right) >0$, then there is a unique $x_{0}\in \left(
0,r\right) $ such that $S\left( x\right) <0$ for $x\in \left( 0,x_{0}\right)
$ and $S\left( x\right) >0$ for $x\in \left( x_{0},r\right) $.

body_md:
\label{R-S><0}For an NP-type power series, it follows from Proposition \ref 
{P-sgnS} that if there is a $x_{1}\in \left( 0,r\right) $ such that $S\left(
x_{1}\right) <0$, then we have $S\left( x\right) <0$ for all $x\in \left(
0,x_{1}\right) $; if there is a $x_{2}\in \left( 0,r\right) $ such that $ 
S\left( x_{2}\right) >0$, then we have $S\left( x\right) >0$ for all $x\in
\left( x_{2},r\right) $. For a PN-type power series $-S\left( x\right) $,
the signs of $-S\left( x\right) $ on $\left( 0,x_{1}\right) $ and $\left(
x_{2},r\right) $ are reversed.

title: Proof
body_md:
We write the relation (\ref{xin-rr-1}) as
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left( \xi _{n+1}-\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n}}\xi _{n}\right) -\left( \alpha _{n}- 
\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n}}\right) \left( \xi _{n}-\frac{v_{n}}{v_{n-1}}\xi
_{n-1}\right) \\
&=&\left( \left( \alpha _{n}-\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n}}\right) \frac{v_{n}}{ 
v_{n-1}}-\beta _{n}\right) \xi _{n-1}-v_{n+1}+\alpha _{n}v_{n}-\beta
_{n}v_{n-1}.
\end{eqnarray*} 
Substituting $\xi _{n-1}=u_{n-1}-v_{n-1}$ into the right hand side of the
above equality and simplifying yield 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left( \xi _{n+1}-\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n}}\xi _{n}\right) -\left( \alpha _{n}- 
\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n}}\right) \left( \xi _{n}-\frac{v_{n}}{v_{n-1}}\xi
_{n-1}\right) \\
&=&\left( -\frac{v_{n+1}}{v_{n-1}}+\alpha _{n}\frac{v_{n}}{v_{n-1}}-\beta
_{n}\right) u_{n-1},
\end{eqnarray*} 
which, by (\ref{vn-gn}), implies (\ref{xin-rr-2}). The formula (\ref{thn})
follows from (\ref{vn+1/vn}), and (\ref{ln}) follows by an elementary
computation.

It is clear that $\theta _{n}>0$ for $n\geq 1$ provided $a<1,b,c>0$. The
numerator of the fraction in (\ref{ln}) can be written as 
\begin{equation*}
\left( n-2\right) n+2\left( 1-p\right) n+\left( a+c\right) +\left(
n-p\right) \left( c+1\right) ,
\end{equation*} 
which is positive for $n\geq 2$ if $a<1$, $b>0$, $c>\max \left\{
-a,b\right\} $, thereby completing the proof.

label: L-sgngn-p
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{L-sgngn-p}Suppose that $a<1,c>b>0$, $p\in \left( 0,1\right) $ and let
$\gamma _{n}\equiv \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) $ be defined by (\ref{gamn}).

(i) If $\delta \left( p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$, $\Delta \gamma
_{1}\left( p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$ and $\gamma _{1}\left(
p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$, then $\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) \geq
\left( \leq \right) 0$ for all $n\geq 1$.

(ii) If $\delta \left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ and $\gamma _{1}\left(
p\right) \leq \left( \geq \right) 0$, or $\delta \left( p\right) =0$, $ 
\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ and $\gamma _{1}\left(
p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$, then there is an $n_{1}\geq 1$ such that $ 
\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$ for $1\leq n\leq n_{1}-1$ and
$\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ for $n\geq n_{1}+1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\Delta \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) &:&=\gamma _{n+1}\left( p\right) -\gamma
_{n}\left( p\right) =2np\left( a-b+c-p\right) \\
&&-\left( c+1\right) p^{2}+2\left( c+a-b+ab\right) p-a\left( a+c\right) , \\
\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p\right) &=&-\left( c+3\right) p^{2}+2\left(
2a-2b+2c+ab\right) p-a\left( a+c\right) , \\
\Delta \gamma _{n+1}\left( p\right) -\Delta \gamma _{n}\left( p\right)
&=&2p\left( a-b+c-p\right) =2p\delta \left( p\right) .
\end{eqnarray*}

(i) If $\delta \left( p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$, then the
sequence $\left\{ \Delta \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) \right\} _{n\geq 1}$ is
increasing (decreasing). This together with $\Delta \gamma _{1}\left(
p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$ implies that $\left\{ \gamma _{n}\left(
p\right) \right\} _{n\geq 1}$ is also increasing (decreasing). Therefore, if
$\gamma _{1}\left( p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) 0$, then $\gamma
_{n}\left( p\right) \geq \left( \leq \right) \gamma _{1}\left( p\right) \geq
\left( \leq \right) 0$ for all $n\geq 1$.

(ii) If $\delta \left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$, then the sequence $ 
\left\{ \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) \right\} _{n\geq 1}$ is convex (concave).
This together with $\gamma _{1}\left( p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$ and $ 
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\left[ n^{-2}\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) \right]
=p\delta \left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ yields that there is an $ 
n_{1}\geq 1$ such that $\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$ for $ 
1\leq n\leq n_{1}-1$ and $\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ for
$n\geq n_{1}+1$.

If $\delta \left( p\right) =0$, then 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) &=&-n\left[ cp^{2}-\left( a-b+c+2ab\right)
p+a\left( a+c\right) \right] +ab\left( p\left( c+1\right) -\left( c+a\right)
\right) , \\
\Delta \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) &=&cp^{2}+\left( a-b+c+2ab\right)
p-a\left( a+c\right) \equiv \Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p\right) .
\end{eqnarray*} 
This shows that the sequence $\left\{ \gamma _{n}\left( p\right) \right\}
_{n\geq 1}$ is increasing (decreasing) if $\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p\right)
>\left( <\right) 0$. Since $\gamma _{1}\left( p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$
and $\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\left[ n^{-1}\gamma _{n}\left( p\right)  
\right] =\Delta \gamma _{1}\left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$, there is an $ 
n_{1}\geq 1$ such that $\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) <\left( >\right) 0$ for $ 
1\leq n\leq n_{1}-1$ and $\gamma _{n}\left( p\right) >\left( <\right) 0$ for
$n\geq n_{1}+1$.

This completes the proof.

title: Remark
body_md:
From Remark \ref{R-C3,4}, our Theorems \ref{MT-3} and \ref{MT-4} may be
stronger than the result suggested in Conjecture \ref{Cj-BRT}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
We believe that Conjecture \ref{Cj-BRT} is valid, which can be proved by our
Theorems \ref{MT-3} and \ref{MT-4}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Theorems \ref{MT-3} and \ref{MT-4} only provide sufficient conditions for
the second Hm-Pm inequalities. It is interesting and challenging to find the
necessary and sufficient conditions.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It should be emphasize that the signs rule for the NP-type or PN-type power
series, Proposition \ref{P-sgnS}, play an important role in the proofs of
Theorems \ref{MT-3} and \ref{MT-4}. From the published literatures, this
signs rule is an efficient tool to deal with certain special functions.
